<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3599fef12305ff52a4bd06e6397366ee20336ab4` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `99ffeb8fa5774c2e0d3ae26ddd75019704c2917f`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #22300 (body; 6061395792, 6062646657, 6064611758, 6066622784, 6066671087), PR #22337 (body, its 4-file list, the net diff `fe98cc63a4..99ffeb8fa5` against `main`), the consumers at objectstack `origin/main` and objectui `origin/main` `fbad07885`, and the head's check-runs. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run. Rendered 2026-10-08T18:59Z.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **The cut sits after every internal consumer of the widened row — right.** On the head, `find` plans at `engine.ts:12160` and `findOne` at `:12468`; both `return`s (`:12303`, `:12575`) apply `rowsWithoutFormulaWidening` / `withoutFormulaWidening` to `opCtx.result` after `executeWithMiddleware` has returned. Inside the chain, in order: `rowsWithDeclaredColumnsOnly`, `applyFormulaPlan`, `expandRelatedRecords`, `resolveFileReferences`, the `afterFind` hooks, `maskSecretFields`, `stripSearchCompanionFromRead`, then every middleware's post-phase. Nothing reads the row after the cut.
2. **It removes only the columns `planFormulaProjection` added — right.** `widened` is `projected` minus the caller's own names, computed before the unknown-plain-field filter (which can only shrink `ast.fields`) and before any middleware runs. The audit redactions (`ensureJudgedColumnsProjected`, plugin-audit `served-fields.ts`) push a judged column only when it is absent from `ast.fields` and delete exactly what they pushed after `next()`; against a widened projection they push nothing, and the cut takes those columns unless the caller named them. Consistent in both directions.
3. **A hook-derived key survives; rows are copied, not mutated — right.** `withoutFormulaWidening` drops by name, so a key no widening added (hook-derived, or an expanded relation the caller named) stays; a row carrying a widened key is replaced by a fresh object in its own key order, a row carrying none is returned as is, and `findOne`'s `null` passes through. Pinned by the engine test's `afterFind` case.
4. **A foreign key the caller did not name no longer carries its expansion — right by contract.** `QueryASTSchema.fields` (spec `data/query.zod.ts:519`) says the projection must retain the foreign key for `expand`; on base a formula projection got that for free from the widening. The PR body states it correctly ("an expanded relation the caller named survives").
5. **No other read path applies a caller projection and is uncut — right.** `planFormulaProjection` has four call sites on the head: `find`, `findOne`, `hydrateWriteFormulas` (passes `undefined`: no `projected`, no `widened`) and `evaluateFormulaField` (passes `[field]`, reads only `plan`, evaluates on a copy). `count`, `aggregate` (its `driver.find` fallback included) and the write pre-image reads never call it.
6. **Public surface unchanged — right.** `planFormulaProjection`, `withoutFormulaWidening` and `rowsWithoutFormulaWidening` are non-exported module functions; `engine.ts` carries no `export {}` block; `index.ts` / `core.ts` re-export from `./engine.js` only `ObjectQL`, `ObjectRepository`, `ScopedContext` and named types. The new `widened` return is reachable from no exported declaration (`find` stays `Promise of any[]`), so the byte-identical built `.d.ts` the dev measured is what the source implies.

**The `id` question (the dev's open question) — A stands; two carriers in ③.** The consumers, read:

- **REST and the protocol:** `findData` hands `options.fields` to `engine.find` untouched (only the stored-metadata body projection edits it); `getData` maps `select` to `fields` and adds nothing. Neither adds `id`; both are pipes for the callers below.
- **objectui:** the console's adapter is `@object-ui/data-objectstack` (`apps/console/src/dataSource.ts`). Its list read (`packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:4841-4845`) and its single read (`:5028-5031`) prepend `id` to `$select` whenever the caller omits it, "so records remain identifiable for navigation/selection". `ViewDataProvider` builds `fields` from the view's columns and reads through that adapter; the grid's bulk executor reads `row.id` off rows the adapter fetched. Every grid, list and record read therefore names `id`. Not reached.
- **Engine-internal:** `expandRelatedRecords` (`engine.ts:11244ff`) appends `'id'` to a nested projection that omits it before its own `this.find`; the only other internal `find` with a projection is `fields: ['id']` (`:17474`). Not reached. The nine identity platform objects that declare a `display_title` formula are projected by no internal caller and by no objectui `$select`.
- **Automation:** there is no `find_records` node. `get_record` hands `config.fields` straight to `find` / `findOne` (`crud-nodes.ts:490`, `:502`) and, on the `findOne` branch, emits `output.id = record?.id` (`:506`). This is the one reached reader: under A, a `fields` naming a formula and omitting `id` yields `output.id` undefined, on every driver. On the driver-sql family that is exactly what a plain projection omitting `id` already yields today (`sql-driver.ts:7336-7337` selects `query.fields` verbatim), so the node's `id` output was already projection-dependent on the production SQL path; on driver-memory (`projectFields`, `memory-driver.ts:2551-2554`) and driver-mongodb (`projection.id = 1`, `mongodb-driver.ts:318`) the plain projection carries `id` and the formula projection now does not. The consumer-side fix is the executor naming `id` in the projection it hands the engine, as the two other internal consumers already do (③.3).
- **hotcrm's `LINE_ITEM_FIELDS`:** not readable from this container; the card's own fix-site text treats `id` as a column "the caller asked for", which is A.

No row-key, link or selection consumer on memory/mongodb loses `id`. A is the ruling's literal reading ("cut each row back to the requested projection"); B would return one unrequested key on the production SQL path against that ruling; the driver-level divergence is C and is carried in ③.2.

**M2, the `security` label — confirmed: drop it.** On `main`: the security middleware's field mask is `maskOperationResult` (`plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:4465`), after its `await next()` (`:4399`), i.e. the post-phase, on the rows the read returns; `FieldMasker.maskResults` deletes every non-readable declared field from each record. `isSystem` is `return next()` (`:2450-2452`), a total bypass: a `runAs: system` flow has no field restriction to breach, so its widened read is the contract breach only. The ADR-0056 public-form grant branch masks after its own `next()` (`:2543-2544`). No code reads `__expandRead` to skip the mask (the symbol survives in comments and as a storage marker), and an expand sub-read is a `find` carrying the parent's context, so the same mask runs on it. A federated or external object takes the same `find` body (`getDriver` only picks the driver), so the position holds whatever the datasource. The share-link resolve read projects nothing (never widened) and redacts after the read. Pre-existing, widening-independent and unchanged here: `afterFind` hooks and the formula evaluator see the row before the mask on every read, with or without a projection (the dev's second out-of-scope note). The seat's relay 6066671087 stands.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22300-formula-projection-trim.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` `patch`, in pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json`, tag `next`). Right: a bug fix in a released package takes `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3), and no published declaration moves (①.6), so the PR body's declaration `no` on its `Clause-②` line (line 2) is the correct one. A response returning fewer keys is a behaviour change, but it restores the declared contract (`get_record` `config.fields`: "only these fields are read"; `QueryASTSchema.fields`: "fields to retrieve") rather than widening or narrowing anything an author can write; `minor` is owed only to a `yes`. Changeset text: every sentence holds on the driver-sql family, where the defect was measured; one is over-general — "`id` is returned when it is named, as for any other projection" is not true of driver-memory and driver-mongodb, where every other projection returns `id` unnamed. Flagged in ③.4 for a one-clause amendment; not a false statement of the fix.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev open question, `id`: answered — A, as shipped.** Reasoning in ①.
2. **Escalated, carrier named — the driver `id` projection rule (option C).** driver-memory and driver-mongodb add `id` to every projection at the driver layer; the driver-sql family returns the named columns only; neither `IDataDriver` nor `QueryASTSchema.fields` declares a rule. Carrier: a `domain:engine` driver-contract card — declare the rule in the spec's driver contract and pin it in the driver conformance suite; until it lands, "name `id` if you need it" is the portable rule. The dev recorded "carrier: none"; a measured divergence between drivers on the same query is a reproducible defect under Prime Directive 10, so the seat files it (this review makes no other write).
3. **Escalated, carrier named — `get_record` `output.id` under a projection that omits `id`.** `domain:services`: the executor names `id` in the projection it hands the engine (`crud-nodes.ts:490` / `:502`, one line), which makes A and B coincide for the only reached consumer. Pre-existing on the SQL family; surfaced on memory/mongodb by this cut.
4. **Changeset sentence (②):** scope "as for any other projection" to the driver-sql family, or drop the clause — on this PR before it lands, else a docs-only follow-up.
5. **Formula evaluation ahead of the field-level mask** (the dev's out-of-scope note 2): pre-existing on every read, unchanged by this PR, not this card's defect; no carrier required by this review.
6. **Cross-lane file** `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/get-record-formula-projection.integration.test.ts` (`domain:services`): test only, boots the real stack on driver-sql; accepted as the door pin.
7. **`security` label:** confirmed to drop (M2 in ①); the label is triage's to change.
8. **Reverse verification and gates:** the dev's ablation (red on both pins, restore clean) and the 69 derived gates are read from the report, not re-run; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts below.

**CI on the head, read by name at posting (34 check-runs, every one completed):** `Build Core` green, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green, `Lint & Repo Gates` green, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` green, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 green, the Type Check lanes (`workspace`, `source gates`, `consumer gates`, `debt ledger`) green, `Check Changeset` green, `Test Core` 1/6 through 6/6 and its `Test Core` rollup green; the remaining labeler, size, claim and card-parity checks green. Skipped, opt-in or path-gated: `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke`. No red check on this head.
